blocker.refined_diagnosis: Re-run after a finding-BEARING corpus became available (revision 2410fae622bb of l9-ci-debt-resolver, finding_count=1, ingested with no limitations alongside the resolver feedback event; snapshot record_count=2). The compiler now produces candidate_count=2 - up from zero - but promotion_eligible_count remains 0. The recurrence report shows why: distinct_producer_count=1 and distinct_scope_count=1. Promotion requires a pattern to RECUR across producers and scopes; a single sighting in one repository at one revision cannot earn a prevention rule.
blocker.assessment: This is the designed fail-closed behaviour of the publication gate, NOT a defect and NOT the earlier zero-finding starvation. The first diagnosis (an empty corpus) has been superseded: the corpus is no longer empty and candidates now compile. What is missing is recurrence evidence, which requires findings from multiple producers or scopes over time.
blocker.classification: insufficient recurrence evidence - a corpus-maturity requirement, not a code defect
blocker.what_would_unblock: Findings of the same canonical rule across at least two distinct producers or scopes, so the compiler can mark a candidate promotion-eligible.

consumer_not_exercised: l9-debt-lsp-contracts exposes evaluate-compatibility / install-pack / activate-pack / verify-installed-pack, but none was run: there is no real Intelligence-produced pack to feed them.
progress_since_first_run: candidate_count moved 0 -> 2 once a real finding entered the corpus, so the compiler path is now proven end to end. Only promotion remains unmet.
